gen-dafont-outrun-future-roboto-slab: Authoritative and synthwave-bright, Outrun Future spaces its letters wide and traces every outline at a constant width, with short ascenders. Roboto Slab is the structured one, packing its line with open-throated a, c, e and s.
gen-dafont-outrun-future-rubik: Retro neon swagger, set wide: Outrun Future draws each letter with an unvarying line and a large x-height. And Rubik, a plain sans, keeps its soft round letters open and readable even when they get small.
gen-dafont-over-there-archivo: Commanding from the first word, Over There looks drawn by a fixed-width nib, like bent tubing with generous gaps between glyphs. Archivo's outward-opening curves keep the text beneath approachable.
gen-dafont-over-there-fs-asap: Vintage-military in spirit, Over There cuts every stroke to one width and gives each glyph plenty of room. Asap is the quieter worker, a sans with open-arc c forms and lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals.
gen-dafont-over-there-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Over There looks like it was drawn with a fixed-width nib, spacious and commanding at a moderate lowercase height. But Be Vietnam Pro, a sans-serif with steel-rod strokes and a high mean line, is the one built for text.
gen-dafont-over-there-fs-epilogue: Epilogue brings curvy, unclamped letters with a tall-bodied lowercase and stubby ascender tips, all on a wire-like monoline skeleton. Over There supplies the vintage-military heading, and Epilogue keeps a long passage feeling loose and friendly.
gen-dafont-over-there-fs-merriweather-sa: Over There has a vintage-military bark, with nib-drawn letters, no hairlines and no swells anywhere. Merriweather Sans has tall lowercase that makes words look sturdy, so a slightly modest size will still hold up.
gen-dafont-over-there-fs-public-sans: Over There is where the commanding, vintage-military attitude lives, with wide gaps between nib-drawn glyphs. Public Sans does the steadier job, a hefty plain sans lowercase with broad open counters on c and s.
gen-dafont-over-there-general-sans: General Sans reads clean and professional, with a pen pressure that never wavers and an x-height that fills the line. Over There adds commanding vintage-military character, and the two keep a steady, confident rhythm.
